title: autotune: add sensible defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: reduce unit token cost and stabilize tail latency for common production workloads by providing sane defaults and automation for batching/caching and quantization profiles, plus basic unit-economics tooling for SREs and product owners. This PR bundles three related pieces: (1) default batching + KV-caching heuristics that can be enabled per-route, with safe rollouts; (2) model quantization profile support and curated profiles for common open models; (3) a small unit-economics dashboard and API endpoints used by the autotune service to recommend config changes.

Changes in this PR (high-level):
- runtime: add auto-batching heuristics and route-level defaults (redwood/runtime/autobatcher.py, redwood/runtime/config.py)
- runtime: prefix KV caching policy engine and cache TTL defaults (redwood/runtime/cache.py)
- autotune: new control plane component to surface cost/latency tradeoffs and recommend profiles (redwood/opt/autotune.py, redwood/opt/recommender.py)
- models: add quant_profiles.yaml and loader (redwood/model/quant_profiles.yaml, redwood/model/quant_loader.py)
- console: unit-econ dashboard and REST API for recommendations (redwood/console/views/unit_econ.py, redwood/console/static/js/unit_econ.jsx)
- docs: developer guide and rollout playbook (redwood-docs/guides/autotune-cost-optimization.md)
- tests: integration tests for batching/caching + quant profile application (tests/integration/test_autotune_flow.py)

Checklist:
- [x] Add unit & integration tests
- [x] Add docs and rollout playbook
- [x] Backwards-compatible defaults (no change to existing customer configs unless opt-in)
- [x] Benchmarks: internal perf run shows 18-25% token-cost reduction on typical chat workloads; median latency unchanged; 95th improved 5-10% under bursty traffic.

Notes on rollout and safety:
- Defaults are opt-in per-organization via a console toggle; global default remains off until two-week canary.
- Quant profiles are additive (profiles only applied when model supports them), and an automatic fallback to FP16/FP32 is implemented on failure.
- Autotune recommendations are advisory by default; an opt-in "auto-apply" mode can be enabled for internal accounts.

Linear & Incident links: ENG-1245 (autotune workstream), PM-842 (product spec). Related incident SUP-998: bursty chat regression during load which motivated cache TTL controls.

Testing performed: unit tests locally + CI; integration test matrix across g4/g5-equivalent hardware in perf-lab; staged canary across internal orgs.

Release notes (short): Adds opt-in autotune defaults for batching/caching, curated quantization profiles, and a unit-economics dashboard for recommendation visibility. Non-breaking; off by default for customers.

merge_commit_message: autotune: add defaults for batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling\n\nCloses ENG-1245. Adds opt-in defaults and recommendation API for cost optimization.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal canary (2 days) -> Stage 2: 10% orgs with auto-apply disabled (1 week) -> Stage 3: gradual ramp with monitoring and kill-switch. Autotune recommendations remain advisory unless auto-apply enabled.
rollback_instructions: Disable org-level toggle from console and revoke auto-apply; clear autoscaler/autotune service flags; revert quant profile mapping in model registry. Steps documented in redwood-docs/guides/autotune-cost-optimization.md
release_notes: Opt-in autotune defaults for batching and caching, curated quantization profiles, and a unit-economics dashboard. No breaking changes; off by default.
notes: Follow-up work: add RL-driven profile tuning (ENG-1350) and tighten canary metrics for token-quality regressions. Monitoring: added alert for >2% drop in BLEU/ROUGE for evaluation suites when a profile is auto-applied.
